Math / Scientific Notation

Scientific Notation Calculator

Convert a finite decimal to normalized scientific notation or turn a coefficient and exponent into its ordinary decimal value. Normalized notation keeps one nonzero digit before the decimal point and makes powers of ten easier to compare. A nonzero value is expressed as m×10^e where 1≤|m|<10. Conversion back multiplies the coefficient by 10^e. The exponent therefore records how many places the decimal point moves, making very large and very small magnitudes easier to read without changing the value.

How scientific notation is calculated

A nonzero value is expressed as m×10^e where 1≤|m|<10. Conversion back multiplies the coefficient by 10^e. The exponent therefore records how many places the decimal point moves, making very large and very small magnitudes easier to read without changing the value. 0.00072 becomes 7.2×10⁻⁴.

x=m×10ᵉ, normalized so 1≤|m|<10 (unless x=0).
A worked example

0.00072 becomes 7.2×10⁻⁴.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Can the coefficient be negative?

Yes; the sign remains on the coefficient while its magnitude is normalized.

What happens to zero?

Zero has no unique normalized exponent, so it is represented as 0.
